notes: Renter households with children means renter-occupied family households with own children of the householder under 18; it does not include every household containing a child.
Large-unit supply counts occupied renter units, not vacant units currently offered for rent, and does not establish affordability, condition, or availability to a particular household.

The family-housing gap subtracts occupied renter units at or above a bedroom threshold from renter families with own children and floors the result at zero. It is an indicator, not a count of households proven to need a different unit.

Margins of error for sums and differences use the Census Bureau root-sum-of-squares approximation. Ratio margins use the subset proportion formula with the Census fallback when its radicand is negative.
Conservative, median, and progressive need estimates are the lower bound, point estimate, and upper bound of the derived 90% margin-of-error interval, clipped to valid count or percentage ranges.
High-need rankings compare Chicago Census tracts with usable denominators; percentile scores are relative, not eligibility or investment recommendations.
